calibration_artifacts.label: CALIBRATION ONLY -- they cannot carry H1
calibration_artifacts.reason: Two, not three: they exist to show that the corrected, seeded three-depth run reproduces, which is a property of the instrument, not a result. And H1's registered threshold says it outright: tiers_required_for_H1 is [120, 300] because 'tier 40 is the calibration tier and cannot carry H1'.

armB_seed_protocol.gap_this_closes: H1's registered statement says arm B drops below its own session-1 score, and the registered margin is a percentage-point figure, but nothing in the registration said how many runs establish the score a drop is measured against, or whether the drop is taken within a run or across runs. That is the same class of gap as the R13 cell list: a number the gate depends on that was only implied.

margin.claim_rule: H1 is carried by the LEAST favourable seed. The direction must hold in every seed; the pooled mean may be reported alongside but cannot carry the claim.
margin.measured_against: each seed's OWN session-1 (depth-1) score, never a pooled mean across seeds
margin.reporting: the per-seed vectors first, then min/median/max of each per-seed margin
margin.why_not_pooled: Pooling lets a favourable initialisation pay for an unfavourable one: the drop H1 asserts would then be a property of the pool, and no single run in the pool would exhibit it. The statement is about an arm dropping below its own baseline, so the baseline has to belong to the run that drops.

arm_A_noise_floor_not_transferable.why: That floor is arm A's, measured on arm A's rows and registered against arm A's cells. It is recorded here only to say it must not be borrowed for arm B.

measured_basis.reading: The two runs differed only in how the model was initialised, and the invention rate -- the class that fails the exit code -- moved by more than the registered margin by itself. A margin cannot be quoted against a background that large without saying what the background is.

armB_seed_protocol.plain_statement: A single seed cannot support H1. H1 is a claim about a DROP relative to a baseline the same run establishes -- session-1 of that very seed -- so one seed supplies one baseline and one later score and no distribution at all. There is nothing in a single seed that can distinguish 'this arm forgets' from 'this initialisation happened to sit there'.

r13_scope.applies_to: arm A rows only. The registered tolerance cells are arm-A cells (learn/1/reasked, learn/1/restarted).
r13_scope.arm_B_within_depth: arm B's live, reasked and restarted phases are identical within a depth (measured in the pair artifact: phase-identical = True), because arm B has no time-gated path -- its only forgetting is across depths. There is therefore no within-depth forgetting for R13 to tolerate in arm B, and no R13 cell to widen.

seeds.each_seed_is: a complete three-depth run (depths 1, 2, 3) of the same manifest and config, merged into its own artifact -- not one depth per seed

armB_seed_protocol.status: REGISTERED as a requirement on any H1 number for arm B. The seed COUNT and the choice of statistic are put to the PI as D-MPE8-06; until that is ruled, H1 stays unquotable for arm B.
armB_seed_protocol.what_this_does_not_change: No sealed number is re-measured or moved. H1's registered margin of 5.0 pp is untouched and is put to the PI in D-MPE8-06 rather than silently revised, because the measured across-initialisation spread is what calls it into question.

within_seed_determinism.consequence: Re-running one seed at a fixed thread count returns the identical artifact. It can catch a broken tool and nothing else, so repeats of a fixed seed are NOT the noise measurement -- the variance H1 has to survive is across seeds.
within_seed_determinism.thread_count_is_part_of_the_configuratio: torch.set_num_threads(6) is pinned in the tool for this reason: the same seed at a different thread count moves the confidence in the eighth decimal, and the abstention threshold sits in a dense confidence region.

cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.consequence_for_analysis: FORGETTING CURVES MAY BE COMPARED ACROSS TIERS ONLY WITHIN THE SAME CONSTRAINT-(b) REGIME. Tier 120 and tier 300 are mutually comparable (both strict). Tier 40 is not comparable to them as a curve. The tier-40-to-tier-120 refusal-rate change is reported as CONFOUNDED, not as a result, and no hypothesis about forgetting may rest on it.

measured.instrument: tools/mp_e8_curriculum.py check_tier(), run over the SEALED tier-40 manifest as well as over the new tiers, so the count is produced by the same code path in both cases

cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.name: tiers 120/300 satisfy constraint (b) strictly; the sealed tier-40 baseline does not
cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.statement: Constraint (b) requires every content word a probe ask uses to be in that tier's taught set. Tiers 120 and 300 are built to satisfy it and the checker refuses an emit that does not. Tier 40 does NOT satisfy it: 8 of its 136 sealed probe asks use a content word that appears in no taught sentence -- 'what rings in the tower', 'how many dogs sleep', 'when does the bell toll', 'what does Mira love most'. So the baseline tier and the scaled tiers are not the same instrument: they differ in a DEFINITIONAL way that has nothing to do with memory, and any cross-tier difference in refusal rate is partly that difference and not forgetting.
cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.tier_40_is_NOT_repaired: Deliberate. Tier 40 is the sealed baseline arm A is pinned against: its 136-row probe matrix and its curriculum_sha256 are what the noise floor and every reproduction claim were measured on. Deleting the 8 asks changes the matrix; teaching 'tower' and 'many' changes tier 40's item set. Both would move the baseline to meet the new rule, which is the R2 failure mode wearing a cleanup as a costume.
cross_tier_comparability_regime_break.what_still_holds_across_the_regime_break: Within-tier claims are unaffected: each tier's own curve over its own delays, and every arm-to-arm comparison inside one tier, uses one taught set and one regime.

refusal_rate_vs_tier_size.name: coverage floor and arbiter were tuned at 40 items
refusal_rate_vs_tier_size.reporting_rule: Refusal-rate change across tiers is reported SEPARATELY from the forgetting curve.
refusal_rate_vs_tier_size.statement: At 120 and 300 items the same floor may move refusal rates for reasons that have nothing to do with memory: more distractor rows, more vocabulary to cover, a larger taught set for the word-level grader to trace.
refusal_rate_vs_tier_size.status: registered BEFORE any tier 120/300 artifact exists

agent_brief: Run arms B and C in separate processes with the same curriculum files arm A reads.
Hash every harness into the registration.
Emit per-arm per-tier results JSON, the four curve figures, and decision.md.
The frozen battery runs once per arm as the regression guard, ELECTRIC off.
constraints_from_the_plan.explicitly_out_of_scope: The coverage gate and the coverage denominator. MP-E9 registered the denominator as the cause it could not address (E23/E25 territory) and G2 forbids specification edits mid-run. MP-E8 does not touch it either.

harness_hashes.note: Hashes are checkout-stable by construction. See seal_basis and the module docstring for the measurement behind it. reseal_history records every superseded value.

registrations_excluded.why: registrations are ledgers, not evidence. Two registrations that seal each other form a cycle no stamp sequence can satisfy, so cross-registration entries are dropped and the fact is recorded here rather than left as a DRIFT that never clears.

also_recorded: sha256_lf (equal to sha256_of_git_blob, proven per file)
seal_basis.chosen: (a) seal the git blob, not the worktree bytes
seal_basis.rejected: (b) a .gitattributes pinning eol -- it changes line-ending behaviour repository-wide, which is a policy decision, not a gate artifact
seal_basis.verification: tools/registration_seal.py --check recomputes both and asserts they agree
seal_basis.why: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means worktree bytes != blob bytes, so a worktree-byte seal cannot verify after commit+clone. Verified on the tracked 1.4 MB evidence file: worktree 1,473,837 CRLF bytes, blob 1,421,862 LF bytes, and `git hash-object` returns the index blob, so the conversion is applied.

self_excluded.why: a file listing its own hash is stale the moment the hash is written; --check can never be clean otherwise. Its content is still pinned transitively by the artifacts that cite it, and by git history.

stamp_ordering.note: git_dirty_sealed is the field to act on. A non-empty list means at least one file this seal hashes is not yet in the commit it names -- the seal is anchored to a commit that cannot reproduce it. Stamping a second registration right after the first is NOT that case, because registrations are excluded from every seal.
procedure: 2. run registration_seal.py <registration.json>   # git_head now contains those blobs
4. registration_seal.py <registration.json> --check   # must be clean at that HEAD
stamp_ordering.rule: COMMIT FIRST, THEN STAMP, THEN COMMIT THE STAMP. Never stamp while a file this seal hashes is uncommitted -- that is what git_dirty_sealed reports, not mere tree dirt.
stamp_ordering.why: git_head is the commit the seal claims to describe. If the sealed bytes are still uncommitted when the stamp is taken, git_head names a commit that does not contain them, and there is no checkout you can verify the seal against.

name: The three-arm duel on the live bench
objective: Measure the true gap between the live connectome agent and parameter-matched frozen and sequential neural language models on all nine axes, under the deployment conditions that define the program: teaching in natural language, real restarts, and probes in words the teacher never used. Produce the program's core figures: forgetting curves and interference curves under identical curricula.

D-MPE8-01_arm_A_flag_configuration.agent_recommendation: run arm A with the bound ON, because the two numbers MP-E8 depends on -- the learn floor and the guarded-absence count -- are IDENTICAL either way, so the choice costs the duel nothing in comparability and buys a non-aborting arm A. But this is a ruling, not a discovery: it changes what 'arm A' names, and arm A is defined by the plan as the ELECTRIC-learn mode that shipped.
D-MPE8-01_arm_A_flag_configuration.consequence_if_off: MP-E8 aborts at C2 on its first arm-A run.
D-MPE8-01_arm_A_flag_configuration.question: Does arm A run ELECTRIC-learn with ELECTRIC_ARBITER_HEAD_BOUND on or off?

D-MPE8-02_arm_B_dependency.cost_of_scratch: a correct BPTT LSTM at 2-10M parameters in numpy is the larger build, and a subtly wrong one produces a baseline that loses for the wrong reason -- which is the failure the duel exists to avoid
D-MPE8-02_arm_B_dependency.question: Add a pinned ML framework to the sealed environment, or build arm B as a from-scratch numpy trainer?

D-MPE8-05_r13_tolerance_cells_incomplete.question: The registered noise tolerance names two cells (learn/1/reasked, learn/1/restarted) as wall-clock-gated. Measurement found a third gated row outside that list: control/3/live/pair1.0/pair_exact flips its surface string in 1 of 6 runs across two heads and three bench versions. Should the tolerance cell list be widened to cover any row whose outcome depends on the 2.0 s speech-act gate, or should the gate be made deterministic (a fixed budget instead of wall clock) so the question does not arise?
D-MPE8-05_r13_tolerance_cells_incomplete.status: OPEN. Nothing was widened. The affected row is a control-arm surface string; cls and src are identical in every run, so no graded outcome and no C-condition moves on it.
D-MPE8-05_r13_tolerance_cells_incomplete.why_it_cannot_be_decided_by_the_agent: Widening a tolerance after artifacts exist is an R2 event. The list was registered before the runs that are now being compared against it.

D-MPE8-06.agent_recommendation: Keep 3 seeds (the same count arm A's clone floor was built on, so the two arms' stability claims rest on comparable evidence), keep the margin per-seed against its own session-1, and do not revise the 5 pp figure until a tier-120 or tier-300 run supplies an arm B spread at the tier the claim is about. The tier-40 spread is evidence about the instrument, not about the claim's magnitude.
D-MPE8-06.consequence_if_not_ruled: H1 stays unquotable for arm B. Any single-seed number would be a measurement of one initialisation, and a pooled-mean number would be a property of the pool that no run in it exhibits.
D-MPE8-06.question: Is 3 the right number of arm B seeds, and is 'drop against each seed's own session-1, carried by the least favourable seed' the right statistic -- and does the registered 5 pp margin survive being measured against an across-initialisation spread of the size now on file?
D-MPE8-06.what_was_not_done: The margin was not changed, no tolerance cell was widened, and no existing sealed number was re-measured.
D-MPE8-06.why_it_is_a_ruling_not_a_discovery: Choosing how many runs a claim needs, and which statistic carries it, changes what would count as evidence for H1. That is the PI's call, not something to settle by measuring harder.

pi_decisions.note: Four rulings issued together. Each is recorded with the PI's reasoning, the conditions attached to it, and what was actually done in response. Conditions that were not implemented are said so rather than omitted.

conditions.1_flag_state_per_arm_in_provenance: Every arm artifact records the flag state PER ARM in provenance, so no reader can mistake a flag-conditional 0 for a property of the organism. MP-E9 decision.md 7.1 is exactly the confusion this prevents.
conditions.2_this_is_not_promotion: Running arm A with an explicitly passed flag is NOT promotion. D-MPE9-05 stays open and unexecuted.

D-MPE8-01.decision: Arm A runs WITH ELECTRIC_ARBITER_HEAD_BOUND ON.

implemented.condition_1: tools/electric_learn_bench.py now writes arms.<arm>.arm_provenance with the flag census for that arm, flags_reach_this_arm, zero_is_flag_conditional, and a read_this_before_quoting_any_number_from_this_arm sentence. The run-level block already said which flags were passed, but it does not survive being read alone: someone quoting arms.learn.learn_correct_live out of a file has no flag information next to the number.
implemented.condition_2_not_promotion_stated: Arm A's bound is ON because a command line said --flag-on ELECTRIC_ARBITER_HEAD_BOUND for the duration of this experiment. The shipped organism still runs it OFF: the attribute is in CANDIDATE_ATTRS, which no enable*() function reads, so no mode reaches it (measured: unreachable_by_any_mode = the three MP-E9 flags; asserted by tests/test_electric_learn_mode.py). Promotion would mean moving it into BASE or LEARN and is D-MPE9-05's decision, with its own precondition, not executed here.
implemented.the_apparent_contradiction_and_why_it_is: Arm A comes out clean while the shipped house does not. That is not a contradiction and must not be read as one: arm A is a FLAGGED configuration, the house is an unflagged one, and the 16 UNTRACEABLE_ASSERTED rows MP-E9 counted are rows of the unflagged house. The duel therefore compares arm A against arms B and C on a configuration the product does not currently run. If arm A wins, that result transfers to the product only through D-MPE9-05.

D-MPE8-01.reasoning: Adopt the agent's recommendation. The two numbers the duel depends on, the learn floor and the guarded-absence count, are identical with the flag on or off, so the choice costs comparability nothing and buys a non-aborting arm A.
D-MPE8-01.scope_note_for_the_agent_brief: The brief says do not modify Droso internals. The per-arm provenance change is to tools/electric_learn_bench.py, the measuring instrument, not to organs/neural_language.py, the organism, and it was ordered by this ruling.

It is therefore left byte-identical (verified: git status UNMODIFIED; git_blob intact) and the new environment is written to its own path, experiments/MP-E8/results/requirements.lock.txt, by the same generator with a --note carrying the reason and date. Overwriting the old file would have been the edit this condition forbids, and would have broken G0-prime's seal.

Added: torch 2.15.0+cpu, setuptools 78.1.0, sympy 1.14.0, networkx 3.7, Jinja2 3.1.6, MarkupSafe 3.0.3, filelock 4.2.4, fsspec 2026.9.0, mpmath 1.3.0. D-MPE8-02.reasoning: R7 says baselines cannot be ducked, and a from-scratch BPTT whose gradients are subtly wrong loses the duel for the wrong reason -- a failure mode no finite-difference test fully clears.

D-MPE8-03.consequence_for_the_plan: The plan's three tiers assume a pool 3x and 7.5x larger than the one arm A ships with. Tier 40 is authorable and sealed; tiers 120 and 300 need new material, which is a specification input the plan has not supplied. G2's go criteria require complete sealed artifacts AT ALL THREE TIERS, so on the current pool G2 cannot be met by any amount of running. Recorded as D-MPE8-03b: who authors the additional items, and against what acceptance rule.
D-MPE8-03.decision: Author tiers 120 and 300 as registered DATA, not as new code paths -- and STOP if the pool cannot supply them without repeating a subject-verb pair.

measured.breakdown: 24 tell frames (all distinct) + 16 QA answers (all distinct by the stated heuristic) = 40, exactly one pair per item, no pair reused
measured.why_the_cross_product_does_not_count: Multiplying subjects by verbs is not the same pool. 'the rain bites the latch' is a new sentence with new semantics; generating 851 grammatical fakes from a 40-item pool is inventing items, which is what the ruling forbids. The number that answers the ruling's question is the union of pairs the pool actually contains.

D-MPE8-03.reasoning: Extending the curriculum is data work. Inventing items to fill a tier changes what forgetting means, and that is a specification edit.

constraints.a: new items use the SAME registered frame grammar (who/what <verb>s the <object>, and QA pairs of the same shape classes) so the shape arbiter and probe construction apply unchanged
constraints.b: every content word a new item introduces is itself in the taught set for that tier, so the word-level grader's trace set stays well-defined and C2 keeps its meaning
constraints.c: the probe matrix scales proportionally from the registered 136 at tier 40 and each tier keeps its guarded-absence and distractor rows, defined as not in that tier's taught set

ruling_second.decision: Authoring tiers 120 and 300 REQUIRES extending the item pool, and that is permitted -- the plan demands 120 and 300 taught items, which the current 40 cannot be. The forbidden thing is changing what forgetting means, so bind the extension to constraints (a)-(d) that keep the definition fixed. Stop again only if the vocabulary cannot be extended without inventing words no arm could ever be taught.
ruling_second.finding_constraint_c_is_false_as_written: The ruling says guarded-absence rows 'scale naturally'. Measured: the registered 24 guarded-absence rows come from TWO item ids (tell1.2 'the bell hangs on the wall' and pair1.0 'where does the bell hang?' -- the same fact, taught twice), in the teach arm only, at depths 2 and 3, across live/reasked/restarted: 2 x 2 x 3 x 1 arm = 24 (measured from armA_tier40_newenv.json, not inferred). It is not a per-item quantity, so it does not scale with tier size by any mechanism I can point at. The distractor rows DO scale (12 -> 36 -> 90 by construction). Reported rather than quietly reinterpreted: at tiers 120/300 the guarded-absence count is an outcome to be measured, not a number the construction guarantees.

authored.authored_under: D-MPE8-03 as ruled 2026-11-03: extending the item pool is permitted; changing what forgetting means is not, so the extension is bound to constraints (a)-(d) and each is checked at emit time by tools/mp_e8_curriculum.py check_tier().

confound_registered.name: tier-size confound on refusal, NOT on the forgetting curve
confound_registered.reporting_rule: Refusal-rate change across tiers is reported SEPARATELY from the forgetting curve. A tier-120 or tier-300 result must not be read as forgetting unless the refusal-rate movement is accounted for on its own line. This is a pre-registered confound, not a post-hoc excuse: it is written before any tier 120/300 artifact exists.
confound_registered.statement: The coverage floor and the arbiter were tuned at 40 items. At 120 and 300 items the same floor may move refusal rates for reasons that have nothing to do with memory: more distractor rows, more vocabulary to cover, a larger taught set for the word-level grader to trace.

constraints_checked.a_frame_grammar: every new tell is an svo call whose surface == stem + 's' and whose ask word is what/who; a lemma that does not take a plain +s third person is rejected before anything is drawn (this fired: brush, catch, sketch, stitch, touch, mix, polish, dry were removed from the lexicon because the rule would have emitted 'brushs'/'mixs'/'drys')
constraints_checked.b_content_word_closure: every content word a NEW item introduces is taught by that item, and every probe ask built by arm A's own probes_for()/probes_for_pair over new items uses only taught words, taught stems, question words or function words. The stem is taught explicitly, not derived: organs.stemming does not reduce 'cuts' to 'cut' (measured), so the frame's declared stem is the trace.
constraints_checked.c_probe_matrix_and_distractors: distractor rows scale at 0.3 per item and each is proved unanswerable: a role_swap '<q> <verb>s the <X>' is rejected if any taught item has that verb with X as its OBJECT
constraints_checked.d_registered_before_run: this block is written before any tier 120/300 artifact exists

authored.construction_rule: Keep the registered tier-40 items verbatim and in their original sessions (moving an item across a session boundary changes the interference curve, which is one of the two figures MP-E8 exists to produce). Add new items to reach the tier: tells and QA pairs in the registered 3:2 ratio, per session tier/3 split the same way. New items are drawn by random.Random(20261103).shuffle over every (subject, verb, object) combination of the registered lexicon (NAMES 15, NOUNS 67, VERBS 79 in tools/mp_e8_curriculum.py) with subject != object, taken in shuffled order, skipping any (subject, verb) pair already used by the tier. Frame: svo('<subj> <verb>s the <obj>', 'what'|'who', subj, verb, stem, obj) -- arm A's own builder, so probes_for() and the shape arbiter apply unchanged. QA pairs use the two registered ask classes 'what <verb>s the <obj>?' / 'who <verb>s the <obj>?'. Distractors at 0.3 per item (12 -> 36 -> 90), split role_swap / qword as tier 40 splits them, each one proved unanswerable against THIS tier's taught set before emit.

deviation_from_projection.reason: the projection said 136 x tier/40. Constraint (a) allows only svo frames, which yield 4 shapes per tell, while 3 of the registered 24 tells are obl/intransitive and yield 3 and 2. The registered irregulars are kept and their shapes cannot be reproduced under (a), so the matrix is proportional per item CLASS, not per total. Tier 40 re-measured through the same function returns exactly 136, which is the evidence the instrument is right and the deviation is the grammar's.

examples: 'what rings in the tower' -- 'tower' is in no taught sentence
'how many dogs sleep' -- 'many' is in no taught sentence
'when does the bell toll' -- the ask uses the stem 'toll', the answer teaches 'tolls', and a QA pair declares no stem to trace
inherited_constraint_debt.handling: reported, not repaired. Constraint (b) binds the extension, not the baseline it extends; deleting a registered probe would change the 136-row matrix arm A is sealed against, and fixing it by teaching 'tower' would change tier 40's item set. Recorded here so a reader of tier 120/300 knows the baseline is not perfect.

tiers.named_cost: The plan asks for tiers of 40, 120 and 300 taught items with the probe matrix scaling proportionally. Only tier 40 exists, and it exists as LITERAL LISTS in tools/electric_learn_bench.py -- 24 tell-frames and 16 QA pairs typed into source. Scaling to 120 and 300 is authoring work (80 and 260 more items, each needing a taught form, probes in words the teacher never used, guarded-absence and distractor rows) plus a runtime that exceeds the 600 s shell cap by 2-10x and must be chunked. It is not a flag. See D-MPE8-03.
